name: Busam
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.source_named: Dongmo Niatebaa, Bernadette Laure 2006. Structural phonology of Busam. MA thesis, Univ. of Yaounde — no online copy found

sources.citation: SIL Electronic Survey Reports, country index Cameroon (Wayback snapshot 2018-08-19 of www-01.sil.org/silesr/indexes/countries.asp) -- checked for a Busam survey report.
sources.note: No Busam-specific survey report exists in the series; only the Atong/Ambele/Menka (2002-076) and Manta (2002-079) reports for the SW Grassfields group.

sources.citation: PHOIBLE 2.0 (phoible.org/languages/busa1251); DICAMES (dicames.online) search 'Busam'; HAL and CORE searches 'Busam'.
sources.note: No Busam inventory in PHOIBLE (404); no linguistic thesis on Busam in DICAMES; no Busam-language hits in HAL or CORE.

sources.citation: Eberhard, David M., Gary F. Simons & Charles D. Fennig (eds.). 2025. Ethnologue: Languages of the World, 28th ed. Entry Busam [bxs] (free 'Starter' view, Wayback snapshot 2025-02-23).
sources.note: Free view shows only vitality/population/family; no typology line; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. 2010. The Momo and 'Western Momo' languages: branches of Grassfields. Unpublished draft for comment (Glottolog ref 33956; overview/comparative/wordlist), ca. 20 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Busam appears only as a tone-marked SIL survey wordlist column (Table 7) and in the lexicostatistic subgrouping (Busam 'clearly the most remote member' of SW Grassfields, p.18). p.12: 'It will be obvious that there is no data other than survey data for any of these languages.' Front matter gives tone-marking conventions (H/M/L/rising/falling) for all lects; no word on stress or accent.

sources.citation: Ayotte, Michael & Charlene Ayotte. 2002. Rapid appraisal and lexicostatistical analysis surveys of Atong, Ambele, and Menka (Widikum-Menka Subdivision, Momo Division, North West Province). SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2002-076. 10 pp.
sources.note: Nothing; sociolinguistic survey. Busam mentioned only for lexical-similarity percentages, neighbour relations and location (Bifang, Ambambo, Dinku villages, Batibo Subdivision).

sources.citation: Dongmo Niatebaa, Bernadette Laure. 2006. Structural phonology of Busam. MA (Maitrise) thesis, Department of African Languages and Linguistics, Universite de Yaounde I.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.access_detail: print only, per the reader; access check: not located online or at Harvard
sources.note: The only phonological description of Busam in existence (Glottolog hhtype 'phonology'); a Yaounde I structural phonology thesis normally has a suprasegmentals/tone chapter that would state whether stress plays any role. Held in print at the Yaounde I linguistics department library (and possibly SIL Cameroon library, Yaounde); Harald Hammarstrom's collection evidently has a record but no file.

sources.citation: Dieu, Michel & Patrick Renaud (eds.). 1983. Atlas linguistique de l'Afrique centrale (ALAC): Atlas linguistique du Cameroun (ALCAM). Paris/Yaounde: ACCT / CERDOTOLA / DGRST. (Busam = entry 869.)
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: Inventory entry with classification and a short phonetic wordlist for Busam [869]; ALCAM lists are untoned and carry no prosodic description, so low expected yield, but it is the only other published primary record.

sources.citation: SIL Cameroon survey wordlist for Busam (unpublished; the source of the Busam column in Blench 2010, presumably collected during the 2000 Widikum-Menka RA survey by M. & C. Ayotte). SIL Language & Culture Archives (REAP), Yaounde.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: Only primary data on Busam besides the thesis; phonetic, tone-marked; would at most confirm tone marking, unlikely to contain a stress statement but is the raw record Blench used.
